Evan: Heads-up — our new "edge-samplekit" that showcases Next middleware + LlamaIndex is flaky in preview (edge) when running the eval harness. Repro steps below.
Priya: Steps?
Evan: Checkout repo, set RW_API_KEY, run `vercel dev --edge`, POST to /api/ingest then trigger eval-runner. Locally with node server runtime it's fine. In edge preview the eval harness reports no telemetry and sometimes the streaming response never starts.
Mark: Which SDK version and sample commit?
Evan: @redwood/sdk v0.10.0 (local build), sample commit d4e4b2. Next 13.5.2.
Yuki: Any stacktrace or logs?
Evan: Snippet: 
```
WARN sdk: transport fallback -> node-stream-polyfill
Error: EvalHarness: stream not opened before timeout
    at EvalRunner.waitForStream (/workspace/eval/runner.js:102:14)
    at processEdgeRequest (pages/api/ingest.edge.js:58:7)
```
Priya: The transport fallback log is interesting — Edge has native ReadableStream/TransformStream; our bundler sometimes includes the node polyfill which then loses on-platform optimizations.
Mark: Also saw auth jitter: on token refresh the immediate next request occasionally returns 401 then retry passes. Could be a visibility/race issue in the auth cache when used in middleware vs API route.
Evan: Minimal failing handler I used: 
```js
// pages/api/ingest.edge.js
import { init, ingest } from '@redwood/sdk'
export default async function handler(req) {
  await init({ apiKey: process.env.RW_API_KEY })
  return await ingest(req.body)
}
```
Yuki: Thanks. Two likely buckets: (A) transport selection — bundle chooses node polyfill, (B) auth store isolation across middleware + api contexts (edge isolates per invocation).
Priya: For (A) we should make the SDK prefer platform-native streams when global.ReadableStream exists and log that choice more verbosely. We can also avoid shipping the node polyfill by default for ESM builds targeting "browser"/"web".
Mark: For (B) I think we need to support a request-scoped token provider. In edge/middleware scenarios people can pass a tokenProvider into init({ tokenProvider }) that reads/writes tokens on the current request context instead of relying on global in-memory cache.
Evan: I can validate tokenProvider quickly by mocking one in the sample and see if the 401-on-first-retry goes away. Will post results.
sdk-bot: Created ticket SDK-5123: "edge samplekit - transport selection + request-scoped auth provider" assigned to @Priya and @Mark.
Priya: I'll open a small SDK PR that: (1) runtime-detects native streams and prefers them, (2) exposes init({ tokenProvider }) hook, (3) adds an internal isReady() + await init pattern recommendation for edge examples.
Mark: I'll update the sample to demonstrate middleware + api route patterns: show await init(...) in both middleware and api, and include a request-scoped tokenProvider example using Next's runtime request object. Also add a note about bundler target so folks deploying to Vercel/Cloudflare use the web-targeted build.
Evan: Quick experiment: swapped sample to use tokenProvider that reads token from req.cookies (same invocation) and the 401-flake went away. Streaming still flaky though.
Yuki: For streaming, can you paste the bundle log that shows polyfill inclusion? The bundler (turbo/next) prints that info.
Evan: Pasted bundle snippet in linked gist: https://gist.github.com/redwood-repro/edge-samplekit-bundle. It lists node-stream-polyfill under packages/@redwood/sdk/dist.
Priya: Ok — we'll update the SDK build config to mark the node-stream-polyfill as optional peer dependency and not bundle it into the web target. We'll also add a small MessageChannel fallback for timers (for backoff) because some edge runtimes don't expose setTimeout in the same way.
Mark: Tests: add a unit that simulates ReadableStream present vs absent and ensure SDK chooses native when available. Also add an emulated edge test for tokenProvider visibility.
Evan: Created a sample PR that: (a) shows await init in middleware, (b) demonstrates tokenProvider wired to req; link: https://github.com/redwood/sample-edge-next/pull/9.
devex-bot: Ticket DEVEX-3120 created to track sample updates and docs changes.
Evan: I'll run the eval harness again after the SDK PR lands. ETA for SDK PR?
Priya: I'll aim to open the PR today, add tests, and link it to SDK-5123.
Mark: I'll land the sample changes after we have the init + tokenProvider API so the examples are aligned.
Yuki: Thanks for the clear repro — huge speedup.
Evan: :thumbsup:
_meta: devex: edge samplekit middleware + streaming + auth parity thread
